critical_steps: Both source families are tight g-frames with exact bound 16.
The printed scalar smallness condition holds for lambda_1=lambda_2=1/100 and mu=3/4.
The componentwise adjoint-difference norm is at most ||c||/sqrt(2), so the printed perturbation condition holds.
A specified weave repeats only the e1 coordinate and has zero energy on e2.
The actual synthesis-difference norm is 8 while the componentwise-difference operator norm is 1/sqrt(2), exposing the missing redundancy factor.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact finite-dimensional counterexample together with an exact operator-norm computation isolating the invalid equality in the source proof.
integrity.unproved_limits: No sharp replacement perturbation theorem for arbitrary Hilbert C*-modules is claimed.

scientific_limitations: The finding refutes Theorem 2.4 as printed; it does not reassess unrelated results in the paper.
Replacing the componentwise perturbation quantity by the global synthesis difference repairs the exact false equality, but no complete sharp replacement theorem is asserted here.
An unindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same redundancy observation.
title: A redundancy counterexample to a woven \(g\)-frame perturbation theorem
